summary: The Radboud Scholarship Programme cuts the tuition fee for a one- or two-year English-taught master's at Radboud University (Nijmegen, Netherlands) to about €2,771 a year (amount still to be confirmed for 2027) and pays your visa/residence permit, health and liability insurance. It does NOT pay living costs. Only about 26 awards exist for 2027–28, so it goes to non-EU applicants with outstanding grades, a clear reason for their chosen programme, and strong academic references.
lookfor: Outstanding results in your current field (grades, class of degree), plus how well your previous degree fits the master's
Standing of the university where you earned your degree
Ambition: the quality of your motivation letter
Evidence of promise: achievements, work experience, internships, volunteering, life experience
Quality of two reference letters, preferably academic
Faculty committees may add their own criteria or hold interviews
cycle: For September 2027 entry: submit your master's application in OSIRIS (with scholarship ticked) by 31 Jan 2027, 23:59 CET; the application must be complete, including English test proof, by 14 Feb 2027; decisions before mid-April 2027.

eligibility.q: Do you hold a non-EU/EEA passport and not qualify for the lower EU/EEA tuition fee?
eligibility.no: EU/EEA students pay the low statutory fee and cannot get this award; look at Dutch loans or Erasmus+ instead.

eligibility.q: Did you earn (or will you earn) your bachelor's degree outside the Netherlands, and have you never studied for a Dutch degree before?
eligibility.no: Applicants with Dutch prior education are excluded (an exchange semester inside your bachelor's is fine). Consider the NL Scholarship or other Dutch university awards.

eligibility.q: Are your grades outstanding (e.g. First Class or a strong 2:1 near the top of your class)?
eligibility.no: With average grades this award is a long shot. Consider the NL Scholarship (combinable), Orange Knowledge-type programmes, or a different country.

eligibility.q: Will you start an English-taught, full-time master's at Radboud on 1 September 2027 (not an Erasmus Mundus or joint degree)?
eligibility.no: February intakes, part-time study, Erasmus Mundus and joint degrees are excluded. Pick a regular September programme.

eligibility.q: Can you meet the English requirement of your chosen programme by 14 February 2027?
eligibility.no: Book IELTS/TOEFL now, or check whether your programme accepts a degree taught in English as proof. Without proof the file is incomplete.

eligibility.q: Can you pay living costs in Nijmegen (the scholarship does not cover them) and show the funds for the Dutch residence permit?
eligibility.no: Line up savings, a sponsor or a second award (e.g. NL Scholarship) before you rely on this one.

steps.title: Check you fit and pick one Radboud master's
steps.why: Scholarships are split by faculty (Science 9, Social Sciences 7, Management 5, Arts 2, Law 2, Philosophy/Theology 1), so your programme choice decides your competition.
do: Open the Radboud Scholarship Programme page and read the eligibility list line by line.
Browse Radboud's English-taught master's and shortlist two that match your bachelor's.
For each, note the admission requirements, English score, and whether it has a placement (selective) procedure with an earlier deadline.
Pick ONE programme where your degree is clearly relevant; you get one scholarship application.
Write down how you will pay rent and food (roughly €1,000+ a month; check the current IND figure).
tips: Relevance of your previous degree to the master's is a scoring point. A tight fit beats a famous programme.
Science and Social Sciences have the most awards.
avoid: Calling it a 'full scholarship' in your plans; it is a tuition reduction plus insurance only.
Choosing an Erasmus Mundus or joint-degree programme, which is excluded.
check: I can name my one programme and why my degree fits it.
I know how I will fund living costs.

steps.title: Attend a Radboud scholarship Q&A
steps.why: A scholarship officer answers questions live; this removes guesswork about your own case.
do: Open the Q&A events page and register for a session (4 Nov, 16 Nov, 16 Dec 2026; 11 Jan, 20 Jan 2027).
Prepare two questions about your situation (e.g. your grading scale, your programme's interview).
Note the answers in your application notebook.
tips: Go early (November) so you still have time to act on what you learn.
avoid: Emailing scholarships@ru.nl to apply; that address is for questions only.
check: I have attended or watched a Q&A and my questions are answered.

steps.title: Build your timeline backwards from 31 January
steps.why: OSIRIS gives you only 56 days after Studielink to finish, and the scholarship cut-off is earlier than the normal 1 April deadline.
do: Write these fixed dates in your calendar: 31 Jan 2027 (submit), 14 Feb 2027 (file complete incl. English proof), mid-April (decision).
Set your own target: submit by 15 January.
Work back: references requested by 1 December; English test taken by mid-December; transcripts requested by mid-November.
Plan to start Studielink in early December so the 56-day OSIRIS window covers your submission.
tips: The 14 Feb date is for completing missing items, not for starting late.
avoid: Starting Studielink in October and running out of the 56-day window before references arrive.
check: Every document has a 'request by' date in my calendar.

steps.title: Create your Studielink and OSIRIS accounts
steps.why: You cannot upload anything until Studielink sends you OSIRIS login details.
do: Go to studielink.nl, create an account and add an enrolment application for your chosen Radboud master's.
Enter your previous education exactly as on your certificate.
Wait for the email with your OSIRIS Application login.
Log in to OSIRIS, open your application and tick that you want to be considered for the Radboud Scholarship.
Pay the €100 application fee for non-Dutch prior education; your file is not processed until it is paid.
tips: Use an email you check daily; admissions may ask you to resubmit corrected documents.
If your card is declined for euro payments, ask your bank to enable international online payments before the deadline week.
avoid: Forgetting to tick the scholarship option; no tick, no consideration.
check: I can log in to OSIRIS and see the scholarship indicated.

links.t: Application fee for non-Dutch prior education

steps.title: Get transcripts, degree certificate and course descriptions
steps.why: Admission must be decided before the scholarship can be; missing academic documents make the file incomplete.
do: Request an official transcript with the grading scale from your university's Academic Office/Exams and Records; in Nigeria this often takes several weeks and a fee, so start now.
Scan your degree certificate (or statement of result if the certificate is not yet issued), signed and stamped.
Collect course descriptions for the courses on your transcript (department handbook pages are fine).
If any document is not in English, Dutch or German, get a sworn translation.
Scan your passport data page.
tips: Ask the registrar for a letter stating your class rank or CGPA position; it helps show 'outstanding results'.
avoid: Uploading phone photos that are blurry or cropped.
check: Transcript, certificate, course descriptions and passport are scanned as clear PDFs.

steps.title: Take the English test and submit proof
steps.time: test day plus up to 2 weeks for results
steps.why: The file must include English proof by 14 February 2027 or it will not be considered.
do: Check your programme page for the exact English score it requires.
Book IELTS Academic or TOEFL iBT for December (book 4–6 weeks ahead; check the current fee in naira on the test provider's site—it changes with the exchange rate).
Follow Radboud's 'verify your English test' instructions so the result can be checked.
Upload the result in OSIRIS.
tips: If you are close to the cut-off, book a date that leaves time for one retake before 14 February.
avoid: Assuming WAEC English or an English-medium degree is accepted without checking your programme's rules.
check: My score meets my programme's minimum and is uploaded.

steps.title: Write a sharp two-page CV
steps.why: The CV is one of the three scholarship uploads and is where selectors find 'evidence of promise'.
do: Use reverse-chronological order: education, research/projects, work, internships, volunteering, awards, skills.
For each item add one line on what you achieved (numbers where possible).
Put your CGPA and class of degree in the education line.
Keep it to two pages; save as PDF named Surname_CV.pdf.
tips: NYSC, community projects and lab or field work count as experience; describe the result, not just the title.
avoid: Photos, date of birth, religion or a long 'objective' paragraph; they waste space.
check: Each line shows an action and a result.

steps.title: Write your motivation letter
steps.why: Selectors score 'ambition' mainly from the quality of this letter.
do: Check your programme page for any word limit or questions; if none is given, aim for one to two pages.
Paragraph 1: the problem or question that drives you and why it matters (one concrete example).
Paragraph 2: what you have already done about it (degree, project, job, results).
Paragraph 3: why this Radboud master's—name two courses, a track or research group, and why the Netherlands.
Paragraph 4: your plan after graduation and how the degree gets you there.
Close with one sentence on why the scholarship makes this possible.
Ask someone strong in English to read it aloud; cut anything vague.
tips: Make the link between your bachelor's and the master's obvious—fit is scored.
Show life experience and responsibility, not just grades.
avoid: Generic praise of the Netherlands or Radboud that could fit any university.
Repeating your CV line by line.
check: Someone who does not know me could explain my goal after reading it.
I name specific parts of the programme.
steps.prompt: Why this master's programme, how your background prepares you, and what you will do with it (check your programme page for specific questions).
steps.limit: Check the current guidance for your programme

steps.title: Get two reference letters
steps.time: ask by 1 December; letters take 2–4 weeks
steps.why: The quality of your two references is a selection criterion, and academic referees are preferred.
do: Choose two lecturers who taught you or supervised your project; one employer is acceptable if they can link your work to the master's.
Email each a short request with your CV, motivation letter draft, programme name and the 15 January target.
Send them Radboud's reference letter guidelines: English, typed, max one A4 page, real handwritten signature or verifiable Adobe signature (no pasted signature image).
Ask them to describe how they know you, specific achievements, and how your skills fit the Radboud programme.
Collect the letters and upload them to OSIRIS yourself (you will be able to see them).
tips: Give each referee three bullet points of things they saw you do; it makes their letter specific.
avoid: Asking a famous professor who barely knows you.
Letters with a scanned image of a signature—Radboud does not accept them.
check: Two signed, one-page letters are uploaded in OSIRIS.

steps.title: Complete and submit in OSIRIS
steps.why: Incomplete applications are not considered, and the scholarship cut-off (31 Jan) is earlier than the normal non-EU deadline.
do: Open OSIRIS and check every section against the document list.
Upload: CV, two reference letters, motivation letter, transcript, certificate, course descriptions, passport, English proof.
Confirm the scholarship box is ticked.
Proofread names, dates and file names.
Submit by your own target of 15 January; save the confirmation screen/email.
tips: Check your email and OSIRIS weekly after submitting; Student Admissions may ask you to fix or add a document.
avoid: Submitting at 23:00 CET on 31 January when the portal is busy.
check: Status shows submitted and I have the confirmation.

steps.title: Respond to admission requests and any interview
steps.why: Admission and scholarship are separate; you must be fully admitted to keep the award.
do: Answer any request from Student Admissions quickly and resubmit what they ask for.
Expect an admission decision (unconditional, conditional or rejection) a few weeks after your file is complete.
If a faculty invites you to an interview, prepare a 1-minute answer on your goal, your fit and your plan after graduation.
tips: Re-read your own motivation letter before any interview; questions often come from it.
avoid: Ignoring OSIRIS messages—an unanswered request can sink a strong file.
check: I have an admission decision or know what is still pending.

steps.title: Get the result and plan funding and visa
steps.why: Results come before mid-April; the residence permit and proof of funds take time.
do: Watch for the scholarship decision before mid-April 2027.
If successful, accept in writing and follow Radboud's enrolment steps for international students.
Prepare proof of funds for living costs as required by the Dutch immigration service (Radboud applies for your permit; the scholarship pays its cost).
If unsuccessful, ask whether you can still enrol paying full fees, and check other funding such as the NL Scholarship.
tips: In a two-year programme you must pass all first-year courses to keep the award in year two.
avoid: Booking flights before your residence permit is approved.
check: I know my result and my next step.

Find recent walk-throughs; prefer videos from Radboud University's own channel and check any 'fully funded' claim against the official page (it is a tuition reduction).

faq.q: Is the Radboud Scholarship fully funded?
faq.a: No. It reduces tuition to about €2,771 and pays visa, health and liability insurance. You must fund living costs yourself.

faq.q: Is there a separate scholarship form?
faq.a: No. You tick the scholarship option in your OSIRIS master's application and upload a CV and two reference letters.

faq.q: Can I combine it with the NL Scholarship?
faq.a: Yes, the official page says the two can be combined.

faq.q: Does getting admitted mean I get the scholarship?
faq.a: No. They are separate decisions, and only about 26 awards exist for 2027–28.

faq.q: Can I apply for February entry?
faq.a: No. The scholarship is for programmes starting 1 September 2027 only.
